title: Formation of Biomembrane Microarrays with a Squeegee-based Assembly Method
protocol: Start with a 4 inch silicon wafer with 100 nm of thermally grown oxide.
Spin SPR-955 0.7 photoresist on the wafer at 4,000 rpm for 30 sec.
Bake on a hotplate at 115 °C for 90 sec.
Expose photoresist using a mask with 1 µm holes arranged in a hexagonal array with a 3 µm period covering a 2 mm x 2 mm area.
Expose wafer in an i-line stepper using a step size of 6 mm and an exposure of 200 mJ/cm².
Bake on a hotplate at 115 °C for 90 sec.
Develop using a spin developer to deposit 2 puddles of CD-26 on the wafer for a total development time of 90 sec.
Rinse thoroughly with ultrapure DI water and dry with N₂.
Etch the oxide in a reactive-ion etcher for 6 min with specified gas flow rates and pressure.
Etch silicon in an ICP deep-trench reactive-ion etcher for 2 min with specified gas flow rates and pressure.
Rinse in acetone, methanol, and isopropanol to remove resist.
Place in a bath of H₂SO₄:H₂O₂ 1:1 for 10 min to clean the surface.
Rinse thoroughly with ultrapure DI water and dry with N₂.
Deposit 1,080 Å of Al₂O₃ by atomic layer deposition at 250 °C.
Obtain a plastic Petri dish with ≥13 mm sides.
Pour out 5 g PDMS curing agent into the Petri dish.
Pour out 50 g PDMS base agent into the Petri dish.
Mix thoroughly with a disposable plastic pipette or rod.
Apply vacuum to remove bubbles until they come out of the mixture (approximately 30 min).
Cure overnight on a hotplate at >50 °C.
Cut a rectangular piece approximately 2.5 x 2.5 cm with a clean razor blade.
Trim one edge down to 1.5 cm by pressing down on the razor blade in one motion.
Clean the PDMS piece with acetone, methanol, isopropyl alcohol, and ultrapure DI water.
Blow dry the PDMS piece with clean nitrogen gas.
Store the PDMS piece in a clean Petri dish.
Collect lipid stock solutions of 25 mg/ml egg phosphatidylcholine (PC) and 1 mg/ml Rho-DPPE in chloroform.
Collect a 0.5 mg/ml stock solution of monosialoganglioside GM1 in chloroform/methanol (2:1 v/v).

In a small glass vial, make a mixture containing 97 mol% PC, 2 mol% GM1, and 1 mol% Rho-DPPE by adding 18.9 μl of 25 mg/ml PC, 39.6 μl of 0.5 mg/ml GM1, and 7.9 μl of 1 mg/ml Rho-DPPE using glass syringes.
Place the vial in a vacuum desiccator and remove solvent by leaving under vacuum for 6 hours.
Make an aqueous solution of 0.1 M NaCl.
Add 0.5 ml of 0.1 M NaCl solution to the vial containing the dried lipid film.
Allow the aqueous lipid mixture to rest overnight.
Briefly vortex mix to create a vesicle suspension, then sonicate for 20 minutes in a bath sonicator at room temperature.
Extrude the vesicle suspension through a polycarbonate membrane with 100 nm pore size.
Pass the vesicle suspension through the filter 17 times.
Store the extruded vesicles in a glass vial at 4 °C.
Collect 700 nm diameter SiO2 beads.
Prepare a 1 ml bead suspension with a concentration of 1.5 x 10^10 beads/ml by adding 107 μl of bead stock solution to 893 μl of 0.1 M NaCl in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Vortex the suspension to ensure it is well mixed.
Centrifuge the suspension at 1,700 x g for 20 min then discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in 1 ml of 0.1 M NaCl.
Repeat the washing step two more times to thoroughly wash the beads.
Add 25 µl of the SiO2 bead suspension to 200 µl of a 1 mg/ml vesicle suspension in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Vortex the mixture and let stand for 1 hr at room temperature.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1,700 x g for 20 min to pellet the SSLBs.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 225 µl phosphate buffered saline (PBS), pH = 7.4.
Repeat Steps 4.6-4.7 two more times to remove unruptured vesicles from the suspension.
Cleave a wafer of microwell arrays resulting in rectangular pieces with 4-6 microwell arrays per piece.
Place 10 µl of SSLB suspension on each microwell array.
Let rest for 1 hr to allow SSLBs to settle into the microwells.
Gently wash the microwell array chip with PBS from a wash bottle.
Submerge the chip in a PBS bath prepared in a shallow dish.
Place the PDMS squeegee flush on the microwell array chip and gently slide it along the surface 5x to remove unimmobilized SSLBs.
Grip the microwell array chip with tweezers and gently shake in the PBS bath to remove any excess SSLBs.
Prepare a 2 mg/ml solution of bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS.
Prepare a solution with desired concentration of Alexa 488-conjugated cholera toxin B-subunit in PBS with 2 mg/ml BSA.
Remove the SSLB array chip from the PBS bath and wick away most of the PBS solution using a laboratory wipe.
Leave just enough PBS on the chip to keep the SSLB array hydrated.
Add 200 µl of 2 mg/ml BSA solution to the SSLB array chip.
Let rest for 1 hr in a humidified box.
With a micropipette, remove 200 µl of solution from the top of the SSLB array chip.
Add 200 µl of cholera toxin solution to the SSLB array chip and let rest for 1 hr in a humidified box.
Gently wash the SSLB array chip with PBS from a wash bottle to remove any unbound cholera toxin.
Wick away excess PBS using a laboratory wipe.
Before imaging, cover chip with a 24 mm x 40 mm cover slip.
Image arrays with an upright microscope using filter sets appropriate for the fluorophores of interest.
Analyze the fluorescence intensity of individual SSLBs in an array using the automated particle analysis function of ImageJ software.
Compile mean fluorescence intensities from individual SSLBs into histograms.
Summarize the intensities of SSLBs found on a given array.
